summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 2.4/590)

data.turoyo: <...> Maḥtənne bayn ʕəlbəke d dawšo. ʕƏlbəke xəṣuṣi bayn u dawšo, kmikasən bu dawšo, mšayaʕʕe l tamo. <...>
data.translation: <...> He put them in a honey tin. A special tin among the honey; they were covered in the honey. He sent them there. <...>

rationale: First finite Detransitive Infectum box; plural undergoer with b-marked covering material. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation; analysis rests on the Turoyo.

summary: New sense 1: bedeckt sein (Detrans.)
rationale: Makes explicit the sole sense already implicit in the inherited Detransitive Part. Pass. examples; no new lexical distinction.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (LuF 2/11)

data.turoyo: Komər maḥatla, frəsla aǧ ǧule w mkasela ṭowo.
data.translation: Sie machte ein Lager zurecht, legte ihn darauf und deckte ihn gut zu.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell (three inherited examples); compact context with a human patient, now recovering warmth.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (92/47)

data.turoyo: W li lahbo mkasela i kurfo, yaʕni u zəha me lqul ʕaynayna ste w fayišo bayn i lahbo.
data.translation: Und die Flammen bedeckten sie vorunseren Augen und sie blieb dort in den Flammen.

rationale: Fills Preterit sense 1 to five; explicit l-marked inanimate flame agent, visible snake patient and obscuring effect.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 1.1/77)

data.turoyo: Yaʕni məd bašilo i labbaniye, kmanḥətila, kəmkasalla, d lə mičək dədwone biya, w ʕaṣriye kəmǧamdila.
data.translation: Wenn die labbăniye gekocht ist, nehmen sie diese (vom Feuer) und decken sie zu, damit keine Fliegen hineinkommen. (Bis zum) Abend lassen sie sie abkühlen.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell (three inherited examples); explicit food referent and the purpose of keeping flies out.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 2.4/6)

data.turoyo: U ḥa d l oṯe mene, məskeno, gmaḥatla hawxa kito b lagan rabo w ʕal i nuro, w kəbʕe mkasela b əšmo d maye, marṯaḥwola, samwola bu bayto.
data.translation: Wer es sich nicht leisten konnte, der Ärmste, der legte sie in einen großen Bräter, den er aufs Feuer stellte. Er musste sie mit etwas Wasser bedecken und zum Kochen bringen. So machte man es zu Hause.

rationale: Fills Infectum sense 1 to five; water is overt b-marked covering material, without a separate culinary sense.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (PrS 67/46)

data.turoyo: Gsamno nuqro, u kalbo, gmičakno bi nuqro, kasayli b qaršo, ṭray ʕayni larwal
data.translation: Ich will eine Grube machen und in dieselbe hineinschlüpfen; dann decke mich mit Heu zu, nur meine Augen lass draussen!

rationale: Thin Imperativ cell, one inherited example; first-person patient suffix, material b- and contrasting exposed eyes.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (PrS 74/96)

data.turoyo: Dmax harke, kasay qarʕox b qaršo, kazzi mamṭenox u bargəl d uxlinale.
data.translation: So leg dich hier hin, verbirg deinen Kopf im Heu, ich gehe dir den Gaul holen, damit wir ihn fressen.

rationale: Thin Imperativ cell; overt body-part patient rather than reflexive ruḥox; hiding is a purpose of physical covering.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (PrS 15/6)

data.turoyo: kle zalṭono, mkasyo i lašayḏe bu pərč, kmazheri ʕayne bayn u pərč, gzoyəʕ ḥa mene.
data.translation: sein ganzer Körper bedeckte sich mit Haren, und nur seine Augen funkelten aus denselben hervor, so dass man sich vor ihm hätte fürchten können.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Part. Pass. cell (two inherited examples); masculine body predicate with b-marked material. The German event-like wording does not change the Turoyo result-state form.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (3/64)

data.turoyo: I laše kula mkasayto bu galdo yo.
data.translation: Der ganze Körper ist mit Haut bedeckt.

rationale: Feminine mkasayto and full-body skin covering complement masculine mkasyo; no new box.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (58/176)

data.turoyo: kḥozat, žġeni mi ṣəṭrayḏa layto, mkasayto qappal pis, xd u ǧulo daḥ ḥyewən?
data.translation: siehst du, daß sie mit nichts als einem Schamtuch bedeckt ist, garstig wie die Decke der Tiere?

rationale: Fills Detransitive Part. Pass. sense 1 to five; bare following material expression qappal pis contrasts with ordinary b-marking.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 2.12/3221)

data.turoyo: Məqḏiwo qayse, i naqqa d nəflowa i nuro bənne, d šəġlowa kayiso, maydiwo ʕafro, mkasanwo i nurayo. Fayšowa tamo, huwyowa faḥmo.
data.translation: They burned wood; when the fire caught in it, when it burned well, they brought earth and covered that fire. It stayed there, became charcoal.

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa cell: earth material, fire theme and charcoal result in one independent context. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation; analysis rests on the Turoyo.

summary: All 36 supplied occurrences were examined. Stem II covering and its covered-state Detransitive account for the secure verbal tokens. The inherited Part. Pass. box already covers mkasyo and receives the feminine mkasayto, not a second category.

Active reflexive ruḥe / ruḥox / ruḥayye occurs with active II; it is not grounds for Detransitive classification. b- or pronominal ebe normally introduces material; 58/176 has bare qappal pis following the covered-state predicate.

Inflected active forms distinguish agent gender from patient suffixes in context: mkasela is Preterit with a feminine agent elsewhere, but JTM 2.4/6 necessity plus mkase-la supports Infectum with a suffixed patient.

The food examples supply purpose clauses and liquid material; no separate cooking meaning is needed. Existing Infectum-wa JL 11.12/6 is not duplicated; its masculine object versus feminine aʕla requires referent checking.

Preterit-wa disguise at 75/164 is already in the entry, as are face veiling, hair covering a back and several pit-covering examples. Alternate Prym–Socin page/text references are not treated as new attestations.

The inherited material’s wording is unchanged. The defective translation at 78/219 is not selected as an example. kasye at Talay 1/371 is documented as a formulaic nominal candidate pending confirmation.

kmikasən with a plural theme and b-marked honey supplies finite Detransitive Infectum under the state/covered sense already proposed in round 1. Preserve the source’s currency/tin reference without silently resolving every pronoun.
Earth covering the fire in charcoal production is an ordinary II covering event in Infectum-wa, not a separate technical sense.
Part. Pass. eyes, history and organ add participant variation to a cell already filled to five after round 1; reader thin-cell counts are obsolete.
Active mkase at 4.I/151 has no Detransitive marker. Abstract content alone does not change the stem or voice classification.
Is kasye in Talay 1/371 a lexical Syriac adjective, or independent evidence for a Turoyo stem I Part. Pass.? No productive base forms are supplied.
Explain maksena versus mkas- at PrS 71/92; does it reflect local contraction/metathesis or another formation?
At JL 11.12/6, does -le refer to the mixture, or to the vessel by a shift in reference? At 51/45, what is the local gender of sefoqo?
Does mkasyole at PrS 26/13 cover the pit or the man? The supplied current example and the verse’s German differ in patient interpretation.
At 53/11, are tents and riders coordinated agents with the livestock or additional objects? The loose coordination does not decide this.
At 58/176, is qappal pis the covering material without b-, or an appositional description?
Jan 2.12/3159: confirm suffix segmentation and agent of mkaseli in the simile beginning Xəd mədli ǧulo; the English covered me must not decide the suffix analysis.
Jan 2.4/590: does kmikasən refer directly to the banknotes or to their container? The covering theme is plural, but the discourse shifts between them.
Remove the duplicated English article
rationale: The definite article is accidentally repeated before hole. The Turoyo and corpus translation refer to a single hole.

summary: Covering material includes liquid water and the agent can be flame; both retain the ordinary covering relation. Concealment or disguise is an effect or purpose already represented in the entry, not an additional sense here.

Hidden history and covering the inherited cultural foundation extend covering/concealment to abstract material. As in round 1, an obscuring effect does not require a second lexical sense. The state at 3.10/113 is Detransitive; the predicate at 4.I/151 is active.
